audit_findings.title: The unpaid $16 million settlement may be counted neither in owner earnings nor the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: If the settlement expense was added back to anchor OE, the still-unpaid liability must reduce the cash bridge; otherwise the obligation is omitted from both OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has accrued a liability of $ 16,000,000 in the third quarter with respect to this litigation, which is reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The $16 million liability is demonstrated, but its omission is unresolved because the OE workpaper is absent. Even assuming the full error, base value falls from $25.67 to about $25.23 and bull value from $29.58 to about $29.14; both remain below the $37.01 market price. The maximum effect is 1.7% of base equity value and does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $16 million settlement through the OE normalization and subsequent payment records; if added back and unpaid, deduct $16 million from the bridge and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Additional litigation claims are unaccrued and potentially uninsured
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured damages or settlements would reduce the equity bridge, while continuing defense costs would reduce future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: It is possible that the Company could be required to pay damages (in excess of insurance coverages), incur other costs or establish accruals in amounts that could not be reasonably estimated as of the end of the period covered by this report.
audit_findings.explanation: The proceedings and absence of an additional accrual are demonstrated, but the filing states that no loss range can be estimated. The record therefore cannot determine whether the omitted exposure is material. The $1.238 million FY2026 nonrecurring legal-expense adjustment also requires review because related proceedings continue.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current dockets, counsel assessments, insurance limits, deductibles and defense-cost coverage; determine whether the $1.238 million legal-cost adjustment should recur in forecast OE, then rerun for supportable loss and expense estimates.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor may retain a nonrecurring tariff-refund benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.003 million prior-period component and $3.353 million total refund; maximum computed base-value effect about $52.6 million or $1.46 per share if the full refund was retained and removed
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring refund retained in anchor OE is compounded through forecast earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Tariff refunds received and or accrued as of June 30, 2026, were recognized in cost of goods sold in the accompanying consolidated statement of income, and approximately $ 1,003,000 of the recognized refund pertained to periods prior to fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The refund's inclusion in FY2026 gross profit is demonstrated, but its treatment in the OE workpaper is unresolved. Removing the clearly prior-period $1.003 million would reduce base value by about $15.7 million, or $0.44 per share. Even removing the entire $3.353 million would leave base value near $24.21 and bull value near $27.87, still below the $37.01 price; therefore it cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.353 million through the OE workpaper, remove at least the $1.003 million prior-period amount if retained, determine whether the remaining current-period recovery is recurring, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be worth face value to common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding or other repatriation taxes would haircut the foreign-held portion of the $137.565 million cash-and-short-term-investment bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If these indefinitely reinvested earnings were repatriated into the United States as dividends, we would be subject to additional withholding taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates potential withholding taxes and says a significant portion of assets resulting from foreign earnings remains outside the United States. It does not disclose the foreign portion of the bridge or the applicable tax leakage, so neither the adjustment nor its materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level locations for cash, money-market funds and Treasury securities; identify amounts indefinitely reinvested and applicable withholding taxes, then haircut only the trapped balance and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Normalized OE depends heavily on a tax-exempt foreign manufacturing structure
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.491 million of foreign pretax income, 73.2% of total pretax income (computed), and a filed $7.663 million DR statutory-rate benefit; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or reduction of the Dominican Republic exemption would raise recurring cash taxes, reduce normalized OE and lower every forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company has a wholly-owned subsidiary which operates in a Free Zone in the Dominican Republic (“DR”) and is exempt from DR income tax.
audit_findings.explanation: Dependence is demonstrated: 73.2% of FY2026 pretax income was foreign, and the rate reconciliation shows a $7.663 million benefit from the DR-versus-US statutory-rate difference. The filing does not establish the exemption's term or durability. Because the disclosed benefit equals 15.2% of the $50.4 million OE anchor, the issue is reasonably capable of materially changing value, although the actual decrement must account for interacting GILTI and withholding taxes.
audit_findings.action: Verify the exemption's legal term, renewal and compliance conditions; build a jurisdictional tax schedule that also recalculates GILTI and withholding taxes, then rerun OE and the DCF under durable-tax-rate cases.

audit_findings.title: Post-year-end executive compensation is absent from the FY2026 run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.400 million combined annual target compensation under the new agreements, comprising $1.700 million base salary, $0.850 million target cash bonuses and $0.850 million target equity awards; net increase unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net increase in recurring cash compensation reduces forward OE; equity awards also create compensation expense and dilution, which must not be counted twice.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the transition and appointment to Chief Executive Officer and President, the Company entered into an Employment Agreement with the former President and Chief Operating Officer effective as of July 8, 2026, whereby he will receive an annual base salary of $ 900,000 and be eligible for an annual cash performance bonus targeted at 50 % of base salary, in addition to being eligible for an annual equity award targeted at 50 % of base salary.
audit_findings.explanation: The new agreements and their post-year-end effective date are demonstrated, but the record lacks the executives' complete FY2026 bonus and equity compensation. The combined base salary rises only $0.027 million versus the disclosed prior bases of $1.673 million, while the incremental bonus and equity cost cannot be established from the supplied record. Materiality therefore remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Compare each executive's FY2026 salary, cash incentive and equity-award expense with the new annual targets; reduce forward OE by the net recurring cash increase and incorporate equity awards consistently with the diluted-share treatment before rerunning the valuation.
